title: pointer
description: point to an object belonging to a template

messages.description: when reaching the end of a list

arguments.description: template names. templates create corresponding outlets plus an extra outlet for non matching templates. If no args are given, 2 outlets are created

methods.description: sets to the canvas' "head" of the list, the symbol needs to be in the format 'pd-canvasname'
move and output next pointer or "bang" to right outlet if we reach the end of the list
get one or more field values. The result appears as a list out the rightmost outlet.
set one or more fields of the current scalar
point to the scalar nearest to the given (x, y) position
goes back to the head of the list and output its pointer (unless the end of list was reached)
outputs the next object (if 0) or the next selected object (if 1) or "bang" to right outlet if we reach the end of the list
delete the current object and output the next (or send a "bang" to the right outlet if it was the last one)
send pointer to a receive name given by the symbol
send any message to the canvas containing the scalar
send the name of the containing canvas to the right outlet
compare an incoming pointer with the stored pointer

body: [pointer] stores a reference to a scalar of a data structure, or to the head of a list of scalars. A bang outputs it, and 'traverse' and 'next' move it through the scalars of a patch, each going out the outlet for its template; the rightmost outlet bangs at the end of the list. Pointers are safe: when a scalar is deleted, pointers to it become invalid instead of pointing at freed memory.
